passage: The hall was crowded and loud with wedding music, and Hrithik's uncle had to shout to be heard. "Pankaj got ninety-two in maths. What did you get, Hrithik?" Hrithik said his number quietly, and a relative shook her head and said, "Learn from your cousin." He looked at his sandals. Across the room Pankaj was standing beside the sweets, pushing his plate around, not eating. Later, on the terrace where it was quieter, Hrithik told his mother he felt small, and she squeezed his shoulder and said marks were not all of him. He thought, I am more than a number, and went to find Pankaj.

qa.q: What did Pankaj get in maths?
How was Hrithik feeling when he looked at his sandals?
qa.a: He felt small and hurt by being compared to his cousin.

qa.q: What did Hrithik do that helped him after the comparison?
qa.a: He told his mother how he felt, and she reassured him. Talking to a parent, rather than hiding the hurt, helped him remember he is more than his marks.

qa.q: How might Pankaj have felt at the sweets table?
qa.a: Pankaj may have felt judged and uncomfortable too, since he stood pushing his plate around and did not eat.

grounding: A child feels small when relatives compare his marks with his cousin's, tells his parent, and sees that the cousin may feel judged as well.

passage: At Bua's flat in Dwarka, Sunday lunch was loud and full of rajma. Then Phoopha-ji asked the question. 'Nitin, how many marks in maths?' 'Seventy-two.' 'Sarita got ninety-eight,' Bua said, beaming. 'Learn from your cousin, beta.' Everyone nodded. Nitin stared at his plate. He felt about two inches tall. Sarita's ears were red, and she was pushing rice into a little wall. On the metro home, Nitin said quietly, 'Papa, I hate it when they do that. I felt so small.' Papa put an arm around him. 'You're not a number. I'll tell Bua we don't do comparisons.' Nitin nodded. Then he thought of Sarita's red ears. Maybe being the one held up wasn't fun either.

qa.q: What marks did Nitin get in maths?
How did Nitin feel when Bua told him to learn from his cousin?
qa.a: Small and hurt, about two inches tall, as he stared at his plate.

qa.q: What did Nitin do after lunch that helped?
qa.a: He told Papa honestly that he felt small, and Papa reassured him and offered to speak to Bua.

qa.q: What might Sarita have felt during the comparison?
qa.a: Embarrassed and uncomfortable; her red ears and the rice wall suggest she felt judged too.

grounding: A boy feels small when relatives compare his marks with his cousin's, tells his father, and sees his cousin may feel judged too.

passage:
'Did you hear Masi?' Eshaan kicked the terrace wall with his sandal. '"Ankita came first again, Eshaan, what happened to you?" In front of everyone.'
Ankita leaned on the railing, her dupatta flapping. 'I heard.'
'You don't get it. You're always the good example.'
'You think that's fun?' Ankita said. 'Now if I come second, everyone will say, "What happened to Ankita?" I couldn't even eat my gulab jamun.'
Eshaan stared. 'Really?'
'Really. I'm not a rank either.'
They were quiet. Then Eshaan said, 'I'm going to tell Mummy it made me feel rubbish.'
'Tell her to ask Masi to stop, for both of us.'
Downstairs, Eshaan found Mummy by the sweets table. 'Can we talk? Masi's comparing thing hurt.' Mummy put her plate down. 'Come. I'm listening.'

qa.q: How did Eshaan feel after Masi's comment?
qa.a: Hurt and humiliated at being compared in front of everyone, so he kicked the terrace wall.

qa.q: What step did Eshaan take after talking with Ankita?
qa.a: He told Mummy the comparison hurt, and she put her plate down to listen.

qa.q: How does Ankita experience being the good example?
qa.a: As pressure, not fun; she worries what people will say if she ever comes second.

grounding: A boy hurt by a relative comparing his marks with his cousin's learns she feels judged too, and tells his mother.
